NS-001.root_cause: Interface Fa0/1 on SW1 is administratively shut down ('shutdown' command present), disconnecting all VLAN 10 hosts from the router.
evidence: Fa0/1 is administratively down, line protocol is down

NS-002.root_cause: PC-B has incorrect default gateway 192.168.20.2 instead of the correct router subinterface 192.168.20.1.
fix_steps: On PC-B: set default gateway to 192.168.20.1

NS-003.root_cause: SW2 Fa0/3 is in VLAN 1 (default) instead of VLAN 30. DHCP requests from the new host do not reach the VLAN 30 DHCP scope.

NS-004.root_cause: VLAN 40 is not in the allowed VLAN list on the trunk link between SW1 and SW2. Only VLANs 10, 20, 30 are permitted.

NS-005.root_cause: DHCP helper-address on the VLAN 50 interface is misconfigured, pointing to the VLAN 10 scope. Hosts receive 192.168.10.x addresses instead of 192.168.50.x.
evidence: IP address: 192.168.10.25 leased to VLAN 50 host
fix_steps: Verify and correct the ip helper-address on the VLAN 50 subinterface

NS-006.root_cause: ACL OUTBOUND line 20 denies UDP port 53, blocking all DNS queries from the LAN even though ICMP to 8.8.8.8 works.

NS-007.root_cause: NAT-ACL uses wildcard mask 0.0.0.254 instead of 0.0.0.255, excluding odd/even hosts including 192.168.1.50 from NAT translation.
evidence: show ip nat translations (no entry for .50)

NS-008.root_cause: R2 has only a default route via R1, but R1 does not have a return route to forward R2's traffic to 10.2.0.0/16 properly.
fix_steps: On R1: ip route 10.2.0.0 255.255.0.0 Serial0/1 (or appropriate next hop)

NS-009.root_cause: OSPF area mismatch: R3 is in Area 0 and R1 is in Area 1. OSPF neighbors cannot form adjacency across different areas.
fix_steps: On R1: router ospf 1, network 172.16.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0

NS-010.root_cause: GUEST-ACL line 30 correctly denies guest VLAN traffic to corporate subnets (192.168.0.0/16). This is intended guest isolation, not a fault.
fix_steps: No fix needed — this is expected security behavior for guest isolation
NS-010.verification_steps: Confirm guest policy requirements with network admin

NS-011.root_cause: Duplicate IP address 192.168.10.20 — two different MAC addresses (0011.2233.0101 and 0055.6677.8899) are claiming the same IP, causing ARP conflict.
fix_steps: Change PC-X static IP to an unused address or add DHCP reservation

NS-012.root_cause: DHCP pool exhausted — all 254 addresses are leased. New hosts cannot receive an IP.
fix_steps: Reduce lease time or expand subnet

NS-013.root_cause: Static route on R2 points to unreachable next hop 10.1.1.9 instead of correct 10.1.1.1.

NS-014.root_cause: Native VLAN mismatch between SW1 (native VLAN 1) and SW3 (native VLAN 99) on the trunk link.
fix_steps: On SW1: interface Gi0/2, switchport trunk native vlan 99
Or on SW3: interface Gi0/1, switchport trunk native vlan 1

NS-015.root_cause: NAT ACL (access-list 1) permits 10.0.0.0/8 but LAN uses 192.168.1.0/24. No NAT translation occurs for LAN traffic.

NS-016.root_cause: WLC RADIUS server IP is 192.168.5.51 but actual RADIUS server is at 192.168.5.50. Wrong IP prevents authentication.
fix_steps: Update WLC RADIUS server IP from 192.168.5.51 to 192.168.5.50

NS-017.root_cause: ACL SERVER-IN denies TCP ports 80 and 443 inbound on VLAN 20, blocking all HTTP/HTTPS access to servers.

NS-018.root_cause: BGP MD5 authentication mismatch: R1 has password CISCO123 but R2 has no password configured.
fix_steps: On R2: router bgp 65002, neighbor 10.0.0.1 password CISCO123

NS-019.root_cause: Both SW1 and SW2 claim to be the STP root bridge for VLAN 1, indicating a BPDU storm or misconfiguration causing a forwarding loop.
evidence: SW1: This bridge is the root
SW2: This bridge is the root
fix_steps: Set explicit root bridge priority: spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 4096 on SW1

NS-020.root_cause: Uplink Fa0/24 between SW4 and SW5 is configured as access port in VLAN 70 instead of trunk, preventing proper inter-switch VLAN communication.
evidence: SW4 Fa0/24: Administrative Mode: static access
SW5 Fa0/24: Administrative Mode: static access
fix_steps: On both switches: interface fa0/24, switchport mode trunk

NS-021.root_cause: Voice VLAN is not configured on SW6 Fa0/1 — shows 'Voice VLAN: none'. VoIP phones cannot obtain voice VLAN DHCP lease.

NS-022.root_cause: Interface Gi0/1 on SW7 is flapping — repeated up/down transitions indicate a physical layer issue (bad cable, SFP, or duplex mismatch).
evidence: GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is down
LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: changed state to down/up repeatedly
fix_steps: Check duplex/speed settings on both ends

NS-023.root_cause: Firewall ACL BRANCH-TO-DMZ only permits ports 443 and 80. Port 8443 is denied by the implicit deny rule.
fix_steps: Add: permit tcp 10.10.0.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.20.0.50 eq 8443 (before the deny)

NS-024.root_cause: EIGRP AS number mismatch: R3 uses AS 200, R4 uses AS 100. EIGRP will not form neighbor adjacency.
fix_steps: On R3: no router eigrp 200, router eigrp 100, network 172.16.1.0 0.0.0.3

NS-025.root_cause: DHCP server service on Windows Server is stopped. Hosts fall back to APIPA (169.254.x.x) addressing.

NS-026.root_cause: Internal DNS server's interface line protocol is down, making it unreachable even though internet connectivity works.
evidence: FastEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is down
fix_steps: Check physical cable on DNS server interface

NS-027.root_cause: ISAKMP lifetime mismatch: R1 has 1800 seconds and R2 has 3600 seconds. Tunnel renegotiates every 30 minutes at the shorter lifetime.
fix_steps: On R2: crypto isakmp policy 10, lifetime 1800 (match R1)

NS-028.root_cause: VTP synchronization issue: SW8 revision number (8) is lower than SW1 (15). VLAN 90 has not propagated to SW8.
fix_steps: Verify trunk link between SW1 and SW8
Check VTP password matches on both sides

NS-029.root_cause: Port security violation on Fa0/5: maximum 1 MAC allowed but 3+ MACs detected from an unmanaged switch, causing error-disable.

NS-030.root_cause: VoIP phones are not marking traffic with DSCP EF — the QoS VOICE class shows 0 matched packets. The policy exists but upstream marking is absent.
fix_steps: Configure VoIP phones or upstream switch to mark voice traffic with DSCP EF

NS-031.root_cause: ACL VLAN10-OUT applied outbound on VLAN 10 only permits intra-VLAN traffic. Return traffic from server VLAN 50 is denied.
fix_steps: Add permit for server VLAN: permit ip 192.168.5.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 (before deny)

NS-032.root_cause: HSRP preempt is not configured on R2. When R1's tracked object fails (priority drops to 90), R2 (priority 100) won't automatically take over.
fix_steps: On R2: interface vlan 10, standby 1 preempt

NS-033.root_cause: DHCP pool for VLAN 100 only provides external DNS (8.8.8.8). Internal DNS server 10.0.0.53 is not included.

NS-034.root_cause: Uplink Gi0/1 on SW10 is configured as access port in VLAN 1 instead of trunk. All VLANs 10-50 are blocked.
evidence: show interfaces trunk — (no ports in trunking mode)
